bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar fish advisory after Nepal floods: Don’t eat or sell unknown species Bihar’s Fisheries Department has advised people to avoid consuming or selling unusual or unknown fish found in floodwaters until the species are properly identified. By CNBCTV18.com September 2, 2026, 11:14:53 AM IST (Published) 2 Min Read The Bihar government has issued an advisory after reports of unknown and unusual fish species were found in some parts of the state, amid floodwaters from Nepal. A large catfish has appeared in the Gandak River and nearby flooded areas. The advisory, issued by the Department of Fisheries, Animal and Fisheries Resources, Bihar, asks people to be cautious and avoid consuming or selling such fish until they are properly identified. This comes after some people reported falling ill following the consumption of such fish. जनहित में आवश्यक सूचना / एडवाइजरी नेपाल की ओर से बाढ़ के पानी के साथ बिहार में पहुंची अज्ञात /असामान्य मछलियों के संबंध में सावधानी बरतें #PublicAdvisory #PublicAwareness #FloodAlert #FloodWater #UnknownFish #UnusualFish #Fisheries #सावधानी_बरतें #बाढ़ #बाढ़_का_पानी #अज्ञात_मछली pic.twitter.com/FRObPDsIZu — Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources Dept., Bihar (@BiharAFRD) August 31, 2026 According to the advisory, information has been received about the arrival of unusual fish in some areas of Bihar with floodwaters from Nepa l. People are also being asked to inform the authorities if they spot such fish. The department said these fish could have entered rivers, ponds and other water bodies because of flooding. It warned that some unusual fish may be harmful to human health if consumed. It also said such fish could carry viruses, bacteria, fungi and other harmful organisms. The advisory asked people to follow these precautions: Do not consume fish that look unusual or unfamiliar. Do not buy or sell fish caught from floodwaters if their identity is not known. Do not eat any fish that has not been identified or certified by the concerned department. If anyone develops vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, fever or other unusual symptoms after eating such fish, they should immediately contact the nearest health centre or hospital and inform medical staff about the fish they consumed. People who spot such fish should inform the district fisheries officer or local administration. Videos of unusually large catfish have been circulating on social media. Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said the fish are believed to be goonch catfish, scientifically known as Bagarius bagarius. They are locally called ‘Gochita’. नेपाल से लगातार बहते हुए ये एक ही तरह की और बड़े साइज की मछलीयां बिहार आ रही है और सभी मरी हुई हैं आखिर ये कौन सी मछली हैं कोई बता सकता हैं .?? pic.twitter.com/nExiYI9ppt — Indian???????? These fish usually stay in deep parts of rivers, often around rocks, where the water moves quickly. It is a carnivorous fish and its diet includes smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic creatures. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar power minister invites investors, highlights solar plan - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 02, 2026 Bihar power minister invites investors, highlights solar plan Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Bihar Power Minister Shailesh Kumar alias Bulo Mandal on Tuesday invited national and global investors to partner in the State’s rapid economic and energy growth, assuring them of full administrative support and an enabling environment. Addressing the inaugural session of ‘Bharat Electricity 2026’ on the theme Energy Sovereignty for a Climate-Resilient Viksit Bharat, the Minister showcased Bihar’s modernised power sector. He inaugurated the Bihar Power Pavilion, highlighting the State’s strides in clean energy, storage systems, and digital grid transformation. Kumar revealed that Bihar has installed over 94 lakh smart prepaid meters, successfully reducing Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses from around 60 per cent to 11.54 per cent. He added that the State recently met a record peak demand of 9,475 MW, with projections expected to touch 19,033 MW by FY 2037. Outlining upcoming initiatives, the Minister announced a scheme to provide free 1.1 kW rooftop solar systems to 2.5 lakh Below Poverty Line (BPL) families in the coming months. Key future projects highlighted at the pavilion included a 1,200 MW Pumped Storage Plant at Nawada, major solar-plus-storage setups in Lakhisarai, and initial discussions on nuclear energy options. “Come to Bihar not merely as investors, but as our partners. Our goal is to ensure every consumer becomes energy sovereign,” Kumar stated, emphasising the need for climate-resilient infrastructure to withstand natural calamities like floods and storms. Senior officials, including Delhi Power Minister Ashish Sood and Central Electricity Authority Chairman Ghanshyam Prasad, attended the event. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 124 SC orders closure of FIRs registered against student protests over NEET paer leak
national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court today ordered the closure of FIRs registered across the country over student protests related to the NEET paper leak issue held from 20th to 25th of July. The court directed that the cases should not be pursued or investigated and must be treated as closed for all purposes. The top court also quashed the FIRs related to student protests mentioned in applications filed by the Centre, Delhi Police, Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Assam. It extended the order across the country. The apex court said, the order was passed keeping in mind the future of students who bona fide came to the protests. The top court also ordered that no state and Union Territory should register any fresh FIR in relation to protest incidents between the 20th to 25th of July. The Apex Court has however allowed the Delhi Police to pursue one FIR against 2,873 individuals who were present in the Jantar Mantar protests as they had serious criminal antecedents. The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the directions invoking the Supreme Court’s special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India. The bench clarified that the order has been passed in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, and shall not be treated as a precedent. The bench recorded the statement of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who represented the Centre. He said, a policy to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide following the cancellation of NEET-UG 2026 will be formulated within three months. The bench also recorded a statement by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) announcing the withdrawal of its proposed protest march in Delhi on 5th of this month. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das told the bench that the decision was taken in view of steps initiated by the Centre to withdraw cases registered against protesters. Meanwhile, the government welcomed the decision announced by the CJP to call off the protest scheduled for September 5. Talking to media in New Delhi, Union Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda assured that the cases registered against the protesting students would be withdrawn and that no harsh action would be taken against them in the future. He said that Centre has also consulted with the state governments ruled by the BJP and are now fulfilling that assurance. He added that the government’s top priority is progress and development of the youth.

national_raw_news.title: 55 mins ago | National 47 Agriculture Minister reviews progress of PM-DDKY; Stresses on timely delivery of benefits to farmers
national_raw_news.content: Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan today reviewed the progress of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) at a meeting in New Delhi. The meeting focused on accelerating implementation of the scheme in the 100 identified districts, strengthening convergence among schemes and improving district-level performance for farmers. The scheme focuses on six key objectives which are increasing agricultural productivity, promoting crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices, enhancing post-harvest storage capacity, improving irrigation infrastructure, enabling greater access to short- and long-term agricultural credit and improving governance and service delivery. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare said that the average score of the 100 districts across the six objectives of the scheme increased from 22.54 in April 2026 to 38.85 in July 2026, an improvement of 16.31 points. The Ministry said that the scheme is being implemented through the convergence of 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private-sector participation. A total of 121 indicators, comprising 74 output indicators and 47 outcome indicators, have been identified across the 36 schemes for monitoring progress against annual targets. The review emphasized on strengthening the monitoring framework to move beyond tracking activities and expenditure towards measuring outcomes and the actual benefits reaching farmers. Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana was approved by the Union Cabinet last year and was launched on 11th October 2025.

national_raw_news.title: 59 mins ago | Sports 33 Cricket: 15-member Indian men’s squad announced for three-match T20I against Afghanistan
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, India’s 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match T20 International series against Afghanistan has been announced. Shreyas Iyer will lead the Indian side, with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. Ace seamer Jasprit Bumrah returns to the squad, subject to fitness clearance, along with Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana. Bumrah missed India’s recent assignments after suffering a knee injury during the ODI series in England in July. He also missed the two-Test series in Sri Lanka. The series will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on the 13th, 15th and 17th of this month. Afghanistan will be the designated host for the series. The Indian top order features a mix of experienced campaigners and young talent, including Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan. The middle order features the likes of skipper Shreyas Iyer, vice-captain Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube. India have opted for three all-round options in Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel and Washington Sundar, while Varun Chakaravarthy will lead the spin attack alongside Ravi Bishnoi. The pace attack will be spearheaded by Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh, with Harshit Rana providing an additional option with his effective cutters. The squad largely mirrors India’s team for the upcoming Asian Games to being at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan from 19th of this month.

national_raw_news.title: "Great intervention": Civil Aviation Minister hails Hub & Spoke operations in Ahmedabad
national_raw_news.content: "Great intervention": Civil Aviation Minister hails Hub & Spoke operations in Ahmedabad Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर "Great intervention": Civil Aviation Minister hails Hub & Spoke operations in Ahmedabad ANI | Updated: Sep 02, 2026 01:27 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 2 (ANI): Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu on Tuesday hailed the launch of hub-and-spoke international flight operations at Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad , asserting that the initiative has facilitated a major advancement in the country's international travel. Speaking to reporters in New Delhi, the Union Minister recalled the shortcomings of the earlier system, stating that the process of passengers exiting the domestic terminal, collecting their baggage, and undergoing fresh check-in and re-immigration procedures was a major hassle. Highlighting the impact of the upgrade, Naidu noted that the new facility represents a significant intervention in international travel, adding that positive feedback from passengers has been deeply satisfying for the government. "For the first time, we have done it from this sector itself, and there is a lot of potential from Ahmedabad also--people flying to different parts of the world. Now, seamlessly, they are telling in their own words that earlier they had to come outside the domestic terminal, get out their bags and then recheck in, re-immigration and everything, which is a big hassle... So definitely, this is a great intervention that we have brought into international travel, and a lot of satisfaction just to get feedback from passengers. So our aim right now is it is a successful model now--to open it up for as many airports as possible. So we have 22 more airports to do, so we will start doing it now," said Naidu. Earlier, the Ministry of Civil Aviation on Tuesday launched Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Ahmedabad , making it the third airport in the country to be integrated into India's Hub & Spoke framework for international passenger movement, after Varanasi and Amritsar. Its launch was attended by Union Minister of Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu , Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel , Union Minister of State for Civil Aviation Murlidhar Mohol and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi. On this occasion, Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu , while explaining what changes for Ahmedabad passengers, noted that until now, a passenger travelling from Ahmedabad to destinations like Paris, Toronto or Sydney had to take a domestic flight to Delhi, manage separate bookings, handle luggage on arrival, navigate immigration queues at a large airport, and risk missing a connecting flight. Under Hub & Spoke, immigration, check-in and baggage check-through will now all be completed at Ahmedabad itself, with baggage travelling straight through to the final international destination. According to the Ministry of Civil Aviation , the Hub-and-Spoke model is a key component of the Government's International Aviation Hub Strategy, which aims to position India as the preferred aviation hub for Indian travellers by 2030 and a leading global aviation hub by 2047. national_raw_news.content: Uttarakhand Journalists' Delegation visits Hyderabad Home News State Telangana Hyderabad News Uttarakhand Journalists' Delegation visits Hyderabad In Short As part of this five-day tour, the delegation met with officials—including Assistant Director General Shruti Patil and Joint Director Dr Manas Krishnakanth—at the PIB office in Hyderabad on the first day. VRC Phaniharan Created On: 2 Sept 2026 12:10 PM IST Comment Share : X Uttarakhand Journalists' Delegation visits Hyderabad A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Hyderabad : A delegation of journalists from Uttarakhand arrived in the city on August 31 to visit sites where the Central Government has implemented development programs in Telangana and to experience Hyderabad's rich heritage. Led by Sanjeev Sundriyal, Assistant Director of the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Dehradun, the 15-member delegation will visit various locations until September 4. As part of this five-day tour, the delegation met with officials—including Assistant Director General Shruti Patil and Joint Director Dr Manas Krishnakanth—at the PIB office in Hyderabad on the first day. Shruti Patil briefed the delegation on the evolving media landscape in Telangana and the extensive information and outreach campaigns undertaken by the PIB and the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) to disseminate information regarding Central Government policies, major schemes, and programs. She highlighted the importance of journalists' participation in PIB-organized events and tours, noting how these facilitate the reporting of significant development stories. She urged the delegation to share in detail their experiences from the Hyderabad visit with the people of Uttarakhand. She encouraged them to help raise public awareness of Telangana in their home state. Subsequently, the delegation visited the ‘Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services’ (INCOIS), which operates under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences. Officials there briefed journalists on India's capabilities in ocean information services, including monitoring ocean conditions, tsunami early warning systems, forecasting, and issuing alerts. To provide a comprehensive understanding of nutrition research, public health initiatives, and the healthcare services available to employees under the national insurance scheme, the delegation will visit the ‘National Institute of Nutrition’ (NIN) and an ‘ESIC’ hospital. Similarly, the delegation will visit an exhibition showcasing Telangana’s handlooms and handicrafts, organised under the aegis of the Union Ministry of Textiles to highlight the sector's role in supporting the state's traditional crafts and artisans. To gain firsthand experience of the rich cultural and historical heritage of Hyderabad—a city renowned across the country—the delegation will also visit historical landmarks such as the Salar Jung Museum, Charminar, and Laad Bazaar. This tour, which includes visits to various Central Government institutions and key cultural sites, will continue until September 4. Daily Excelsior 04:11 AM Sep 02, 2026 IST Dr Zabeer Ahmed, Director, CSIR-IIIM and visiting media delegation posing for a photograph. Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Sept 1: A media delegation from Gujarat coordinated by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Government of India, visited the CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (CSIR-IIIM), Jammu, on Tuesday, getting a first-hand glimpse of the institute’s work in drug discovery, medicinal and aromatic plants, biotechnology, farmer-oriented technologies and startup development. The delegation, comprising journalists and media professionals from Gujarat representing newspapers, television channels and digital media platforms, interacted with scientists and visited key research facilities to understand how scientific research is being taken from the laboratory to the field and ultimately towards commercialisation and societal applications. Advertisement During the visit, Dr Zabeer Ahmed, Director, CSIR-IIIM Jammu and CSIR-NBRI, Lucknow, gave a detailed presentation on the institute’s research programmes, scientific achievements, societal missions and innovation ecosystem. In his address, Dr Ahmed highlighted that CSIR-IIIM works at the interface of biodiversity, traditional knowledge and modern medicine, with a major focus on natural products, medicinal and aromatic plants and drug discovery. Dr Ahmed also highlighted the institute’s work under the Aroma Mission and Floriculture Mission, including its contribution to the lavender-based Purple Revolution. He further spoke about the institute’s work across different geo-climatic zones of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, its support to startups and young innovators, and efforts to strengthen the interface between science, industry, agriculture and society. The delegation was also briefed about CSIR-IIIM’s advanced scientific infrastructure. The institute’s work with farmers was another major focus of the visit. The delegation was also briefed about CSIR-IIIM’s growing startup and innovation ecosystem through its BioNEST Incubator and Atal Incubation Centre. Later, the delegation visited the institute’s major research facilities, including the Herbarium, GLP Animal House, cGMP Facility, Fermentation Facility and Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA/QC) Facility. Scientists explained the functioning and significance of these facilities and their role in supporting research, pre-clinical testing, quality control, drug manufacturing and scale-up of technologies. Earlier, Dr Saurabh Saran, PI, BioNEST IIIM-TBI, presented a welcome address, followed by a presentation on the Aroma and Floriculture Missions by Dr Suphla B Gupta, Nodal Aroma Mission.
